Do not call present just to list edited source files, or run commands to check whether a diff view will appear. tools.description: Declare existing files as final deliverables for the user. Use it when the user needs a separate file, especially Office documents, spreadsheets, and slide decks; prefer your final response when that suffices. The user opens the current files; their contents are not copied.

tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "Get-Process" → "List running processes".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap; on expiry the command moves to the background as a job instead of being killed.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact command the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

tools.name: subagent

The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool starts an independently managed subagent and immediately returns its id. The runtime notifies you when it finishes. The child reports results with `send_message`; use `send_message` to steer it while running or continue its conversation after it finishes.

tools.name: subagent_fork
tools.description: Delegate a task to a subagent that inherits this conversation: a child agent seeded with all completed turns so far (it does not see the current in-flight turn). Use this when the subtask builds on this conversation's context — a follow-up analysis, a review, a continuation — without consuming this conversation's context for the work itself. You receive its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool starts an independently managed subagent and immediately returns its id. The runtime notifies you when it finishes. The child reports results with `send_message`; use `send_message` to steer it while running or continue its conversation after it finishes.

cwd.description: Initial child working directory. Relative paths use your current directory; omitted inherits it. Later directory changes in either agent are independent.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

<system-reminder>
Additional instructions from: original source code\AGENTS.md

These instructions apply to work under `original source code`. Use them as guidance when relevant; more specific instructions take precedence. They do not override system, developer, or direct user instructions.

# AGENTS.md

Guidance for AI agents working in this repository. Super Productivity is a todo and time-tracking app on Angular + Electron + Capacitor.

## Repo map

Start with the [repository content map](docs/repository-map.md) (task keywords, code entry points, focused tests) and follow only the relevant links. Layer boundaries: [app map](src/app/README.md). Package ownership and checks: [packages](packages/README.md).

Read by section, not whole: the long sync docs open with a **Sections** index and `ARCHITECTURE-DECISIONS.md` with a **Decisions** index; for any long doc, `rg -n '^#{1,3} ' <file>` gives line numbers for `sed -n`. For large source files, `rg -n` first, then read the range.

## Product principles

- **Avoid feature creep:** extend existing building blocks; new UI, settings and sync surface must make users faster. A personal deep-work tool, not team management or reporting. Surface the leaner alternative when scope outgrows the problem.
- **Less noise, more depth:** no constant alerts, vanity dashboards, streaks or dopamine loops. Attention-grabbing behavior ships off by default; reminders stay opt-in.
- **Adapt, don't impose:** one calm default; add a setting only when real workflows diverge. Prefer not building a feature over adding a toggle to dodge a decision.
- **Privacy & offline first:** no analytics, tracking or telemetry; user data stays local unless explicitly synced. Core tasks and time tracking work offline; sync and integrations are optional and degrade gracefully.

## Required reading per task

- Styling → [`docs/styling-guide.md`](docs/styling-guide.md); user-facing functionality → [`docs/documentation-guide.md`](docs/documentation-guide.md)
- Sync, op-log, vector clocks → [sync index](docs/sync-and-op-log/README.md), then only the relevant contracts. Effects/reducers/bulk dispatch touching synced state → [`contributor-sync-model.md`](docs/sync-and-op-log/contributor-sync-model.md). Judging whether a sync bug is real / how severe → [`sync-severity-triage.md`](docs/sync-and-op-log/sync-severity-triage.md)
- E2E tests → [`e2e/AGENTS.md`](e2e/AGENTS.md); marketing videos → [`e2e/store-video/AGENTS.md`](e2e/store-video/AGENTS.md)
- Load-bearing decisions → [`ARCHITECTURE-DECISIONS.md`](ARCHITECTURE-DECISIONS.md)
- Designing a user-facing feature or writing its plan → [`docs/feature-review-guide.md`](docs/feature-review-guide.md) § Does it earn its place? and § Prior art
- Reviewing a feature or PR → [`docs/feature-review-guide.md`](docs/feature-review-guide.md); editing a type in `packages/plugin-api/`, `packages/shared-schema/`, `packages/sync-core/`, `src/app/op-log/core/`, or a model a `MODEL_CONFIGS` slice persists → its § Long-term cost of a change

## Core commands

**Run `npm run checkFile <file...>` on every modified `.ts` or `.scss` file before reporting work as done** (pass all files in one call). If root ESLint ignores a file (e.g. in a package), use formatting plus that package's checks in [packages/README.md](packages/README.md#validation); an ignored file is not a lint pass. Regenerate generated files through their owner script.

```bash
npm run checkFile <files...>   # prettier + lint
npm run prettier               # multi-file format
npm run lint                   # multi-file lint
npm test                       # shared packages + release tooling + Angular specs (Berlin, LA subset; CI: test:ci, full LA)
npm run test:affected          # Angular specs importing files changed vs master (Berlin + LA subset); `-- --list` to preview
npm run test:file <filepath>   # single Angular spec; package tests use package scripts
npm run test:electron          # main-process tests are electron/*.test.cjs; a .spec.ts there never runs
npm run e2e                    # browser E2E, excludes SuperSync/WebDAV
npm run e2e:file <path> -- --retries=0             # single non-sync E2E; add --grep "name"
npm run e2e:supersync:file <path> -- --retries=0   # starts and requires SuperSync
npm run e2e:webdav:file <path> -- --retries=0      # starts and requires WebDAV
npm start                      # Electron dev
npm run startFrontend          # web dev, generates environment constants first
npm run dist                   # validated Electron distribution for the host platform
```

While iterating on app code, use `npm run test:affected` instead of a full `npm test`. It covers Angular specs only: after editing `packages/*` also run that package's tests, and run `npm test` before opening a PR. It follows static imports, templates and styles; test setup, configs and unimported assets/styles trigger a full run. "Nothing to run" means nothing was tested. CI runs everything (`test:ci`).

For full provider suites prefer the [scheduled E2E workflow](.github/workflows/e2e-scheduled.yml) (`grep` filters SuperSync; `webdav_grep` + `run_webdav` for WebDAV); focused local runs and provider-switch prerequisites are in [e2e/AGENTS.md](e2e/AGENTS.md) (they need both servers and both flags, else they silently skip). Skipped tests do not validate a fix.

`tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` validates nothing (root config has `files: []`); use the app/spec/Electron config or package checks ([why](docs/hardening-earns-its-place.md#the-three-failure-modes-worth-remembering)).

## Project rules

- **Translations:** `T` holds keys; render with the translate pipe or `TranslateService`. Edit only `en.json`, except when adding placeholders: then update every existing translation to interpolate them. See [translation workflow](docs/TRANSLATING.md).
- **Dependencies:** never add packages to the root `dependencies`/`devDependencies`; use platform APIs, existing packages or a small in-repo implementation. A plugin may add a necessary dependency isolated to that plugin.
- **Electron:** check `IS_ELECTRON` before using Electron-specific APIs.
- **Templates & styling:** plain HTML, minimal CSS/classes, Angular Material sparingly ([styling guide](docs/styling-guide.md)). Never restyle Angular Material or shared `src/app/ui/` components for a one-off (local `.mat-*`, `.mdc-*`, `button[mat-*]` or component-internal overrides, re-declared theme styles); use existing inputs/classes/tokens/theme variables, or make the variant reusable in the shared style layer.
- **State:** never mutate NgRx state — reducers return new objects. Prefer Signals to Observables.
- **Tests:** add unit tests for new services and state logic.
- **Service size:** ≤ 1200 physical lines per `*.service.ts` (specs exempt; ESLint `max-lines`). Split by responsibility before crossing; never grow grandfathered offenders — the per-file caps pinned in `eslint.config.js` may only go down.
- **Agent-control files:** modify `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.agents/**` or `.codex/**` only when the user explicitly asks in the current task; keep it in a dedicated commit/PR that says how it changes agent behavior. Incident-derived rules here are invariant + enforcement + issue/doc pointer only (narrative goes to `docs/`; this file must stay skimmable); date cited statistics ("measured YYYY-MM").
- **Hardening needs evidence:** grep for an observed instance before adding a guard; zero instances → record a gap instead. Allowlists only shrink (fix false positives or scope a justified disable). Verify a check can fail before trusting a pass. [Evidence](docs/hardening-earns-its-place.md).
- **Does it earn its place?** Verify demand before judging implementation; decline a correct feature that adds unjustified complexity. [Review guide](docs/feature-review-guide.md).
- **Code review:** assess maintenance cost, dependencies, scale and cross-client behavior; on every change touching persisted models, the sync wire or public/plugin APIs, check them explicitly, however small. [Long-term cost](docs/feature-review-guide.md#long-term-cost-of-a-change).
- **Task component is a hot path:** `src/app/features/tasks/task/task.component.*` renders once per task in long lists; double-check every change for performance impact — no template function/getter calls, no extra change detection, no uncleaned subscriptions; verify against a large task list.

## Sync-correctness rules

These apply to all state-related work. **One user intent = one op; replayed/remote ops must not re-trigger effects.** Read [the contributor model](docs/sync-and-op-log/contributor-sync-model.md) before editing. Sync changes are high-risk: check replay determinism, concurrent/remote edits, vector-clock conflicts and data-loss modes; report material risks before marking work done.

- **Released clients:** `master` auto-publishes to Play internal, Snap `edge` and `supersync:latest`. Prove release inclusion with `git tag --contains`; an unreproduced finding is not a false one. [Severity triage](docs/sync-and-op-log/sync-severity-triage.md).
- **Reproduce first:** every sync change starts from a reproducible failure with real data shapes, not a mocked seam. A sync bug fix needs an exact E2E reproduction written first (fails without the fix, passes with it); unit tests may supplement it. Only app-unreachable server internals or providers without an E2E harness may use the narrowest real-path test instead — say why in the PR. Question unreproducible hardening rather than adding guards.

1. **Effects inject `LOCAL_ACTIONS`**, never `Actions` (`ALL_ACTIONS` only for the op-log capture effect; remote archive side effects → `ArchiveOperationHandler`). Lint: `no-actions-in-effects`. → `src/app/util/local-actions.token.ts`.

# AGENTS.md

Guidance for AI agents working in this repository. Super Productivity is a todo and time-tracking app on Angular + Electron + Capacitor.

## Repo map

Start with the [repository content map](docs/repository-map.md) (task keywords, code entry points, focused tests) and follow only the relevant links. Layer boundaries: [app map](src/app/README.md). Package ownership and checks: [packages](packages/README.md).

Read by section, not whole: the long sync docs open with a **Sections** index and `ARCHITECTURE-DECISIONS.md` with a **Decisions** index; for any long doc, `rg -n '^#{1,3} ' <file>` gives line numbers for `sed -n`. For large source files, `rg -n` first, then read the range.

## Product principles

- **Avoid feature creep:** extend existing building blocks; new UI, settings and sync surface must make users faster. A personal deep-work tool, not team management or reporting. Surface the leaner alternative when scope outgrows the problem.
- **Less noise, more depth:** no constant alerts, vanity dashboards, streaks or dopamine loops. Attention-grabbing behavior ships off by default; reminders stay opt-in.
- **Adapt, don't impose:** one calm default; add a setting only when real workflows diverge. Prefer not building a feature over adding a toggle to dodge a decision.
- **Privacy & offline first:** no analytics, tracking or telemetry; user data stays local unless explicitly synced. Core tasks and time tracking work offline; sync and integrations are optional and degrade gracefully.

## Required reading per task

- Styling → [`docs/styling-guide.md`](docs/styling-guide.md); user-facing functionality → [`docs/documentation-guide.md`](docs/documentation-guide.md)
- Sync, op-log, vector clocks → [sync index](docs/sync-and-op-log/README.md), then only the relevant contracts. Effects/reducers/bulk dispatch touching synced state → [`contributor-sync-model.md`](docs/sync-and-op-log/contributor-sync-model.md). Judging whether a sync bug is real / how severe → [`sync-severity-triage.md`](docs/sync-and-op-log/sync-severity-triage.md)
- E2E tests → [`e2e/AGENTS.md`](e2e/AGENTS.md); marketing videos → [`e2e/store-video/AGENTS.md`](e2e/store-video/AGENTS.md)
- Load-bearing decisions → [`ARCHITECTURE-DECISIONS.md`](ARCHITECTURE-DECISIONS.md)
- Designing a user-facing feature or writing its plan → [`docs/feature-review-guide.md`](docs/feature-review-guide.md) § Does it earn its place? and § Prior art
- Reviewing a feature or PR → [`docs/feature-review-guide.md`](docs/feature-review-guide.md); editing a type in `packages/plugin-api/`, `packages/shared-schema/`, `packages/sync-core/`, `src/app/op-log/core/`, or a model a `MODEL_CONFIGS` slice persists → its § Long-term cost of a change

## Core commands

**Run `npm run checkFile <file...>` on every modified `.ts` or `.scss` file before reporting work as done** (pass all files in one call). If root ESLint ignores a file (e.g. in a package), use formatting plus that package's checks in [packages/README.md](packages/README.md#validation); an ignored file is not a lint pass. Regenerate generated files through their owner script.

```bash
npm run checkFile <files...>   # prettier + lint
npm run prettier               # multi-file format
npm run lint                   # multi-file lint
npm test                       # shared packages + release tooling + Angular specs (Berlin, LA subset; CI: test:ci, full LA)
npm run test:affected          # Angular specs importing files changed vs master (Berlin + LA subset); `-- --list` to preview
npm run test:file <filepath>   # single Angular spec; package tests use package scripts
npm run test:electron          # main-process tests are electron/*.test.cjs; a .spec.ts there never runs
npm run e2e                    # browser E2E, excludes SuperSync/WebDAV
npm run e2e:file <path> -- --retries=0             # single non-sync E2E; add --grep "name"
npm run e2e:supersync:file <path> -- --retries=0   # starts and requires SuperSync
npm run e2e:webdav:file <path> -- --retries=0      # starts and requires WebDAV
npm start                      # Electron dev
npm run startFrontend          # web dev, generates environment constants first
npm run dist                   # validated Electron distribution for the host platform
```

While iterating on app code, use `npm run test:affected` instead of a full `npm test`. It covers Angular specs only: after editing `packages/*` also run that package's tests, and run `npm test` before opening a PR. It follows static imports, templates and styles; test setup, configs and unimported assets/styles trigger a full run. "Nothing to run" means nothing was tested. CI runs everything (`test:ci`).

For full provider suites prefer the [scheduled E2E workflow](.github/workflows/e2e-scheduled.yml) (`grep` filters SuperSync; `webdav_grep` + `run_webdav` for WebDAV); focused local runs and provider-switch prerequisites are in [e2e/AGENTS.md](e2e/AGENTS.md) (they need both servers and both flags, else they silently skip). Skipped tests do not validate a fix.

`tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` validates nothing (root config has `files: []`); use the app/spec/Electron config or package checks ([why](docs/hardening-earns-its-place.md#the-three-failure-modes-worth-remembering)).

## Project rules

- **Translations:** `T` holds keys; render with the translate pipe or `TranslateService`. Edit only `en.json`, except when adding placeholders: then update every existing translation to interpolate them. See [translation workflow](docs/TRANSLATING.md).
- **Dependencies:** never add packages to the root `dependencies`/`devDependencies`; use platform APIs, existing packages or a small in-repo implementation. A plugin may add a necessary dependency isolated to that plugin.
- **Electron:** check `IS_ELECTRON` before using Electron-specific APIs.
- **Templates & styling:** plain HTML, minimal CSS/classes, Angular Material sparingly ([styling guide](docs/styling-guide.md)). Never restyle Angular Material or shared `src/app/ui/` components for a one-off (local `.mat-*`, `.mdc-*`, `button[mat-*]` or component-internal overrides, re-declared theme styles); use existing inputs/classes/tokens/theme variables, or make the variant reusable in the shared style layer.
- **State:** never mutate NgRx state — reducers return new objects. Prefer Signals to Observables.
- **Tests:** add unit tests for new services and state logic.
- **Service size:** ≤ 1200 physical lines per `*.service.ts` (specs exempt; ESLint `max-lines`). Split by responsibility before crossing; never grow grandfathered offenders — the per-file caps pinned in `eslint.config.js` may only go down.
- **Agent-control files:** modify `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.agents/**` or `.codex/**` only when the user explicitly asks in the current task; keep it in a dedicated commit/PR that says how it changes agent behavior. - **Does it earn its place?** Verify demand before judging implementation; decline a correct feature that adds unjustified complexity. [Review guide](docs/feature-review-guide.md).
- **Code review:** assess maintenance cost, dependencies, scale and cross-client behavior; on every change touching persisted models, the sync wire or public/plugin APIs, check them explicitly, however small. [Long-term cost](docs/feature-review-guide.md#long-term-cost-of-a-change).
- **Task component is a hot path:** `src/app/features/tasks/task/task.component.*` renders once per task in long lists; double-check every change for performance impact — no template function/getter calls, no extra change detection, no uncleaned subscriptions; verify against a large task list.

1: // Types for Super Productivity Plugin API
2: // This package provides TypeScript types for developing plugins
3: 
4: import {
5:   IssueProviderManifestConfig,
6:   IssueProviderPluginDefinition,
7:   PluginHttpOptions,
8: } from './issue-provider-types';
9: 
10: export interface PluginMenuEntryCfg {
11:   pluginId: string;
12:   label: string;
13:   icon?: string;
14:   onClick: () => void;
15: }
16: 
17: export type PluginTaskContextMenuTarget = 'TASK' | 'SUBTASK';
18: 
19: export interface PluginTaskContextMenuContext {
20:   readonly taskId: string;
21: }
22: 
23: /**
24:  * A plugin action shown in the task context menu's dedicated plugin submenu.
25:  * Register from plugin.js; callback registrations are not supported in iframe
26:  * index.html files.
27:  */
28: export interface PluginTaskContextMenuEntryCfg {
29:   /** Unique within this plugin. */
30:   id: string;
31:   /** A non-empty action label of at most 80 characters. */
32:   label: string;
33:   /** Optional Material icon ligature name. Custom SVG assets are not supported. */
34:   icon?: string;
35:   /** Defaults to both regular tasks and subtasks when omitted; an empty array is invalid. */
36:   showFor?: readonly PluginTaskContextMenuTarget[];
37:   onClick: (context: PluginTaskContextMenuContext) => void | Promise<void>;
38: }
39: 
40: export enum PluginHooks {
41:   TASK_CREATED = 'taskCreated',
42:   TASK_COMPLETE = 'taskComplete',
43:   TASK_UPDATE = 'taskUpdate',
44:   TASK_DELETE = 'taskDelete',
45:   CURRENT_TASK_CHANGE = 'currentTaskChange',
46:   FINISH_DAY = 'finishDay',
47:   LANGUAGE_CHANGE = 'languageChange',
48:   PERSISTED_DATA_CHANGED = 'persistedDataChanged',
49:   ACTION = 'action',
50:   ANY_TASK_UPDATE = 'anyTaskUpdate',
51:   PROJECT_LIST_UPDATE = 'projectListUpdate',
52:   WORK_CONTEXT_CHANGE = 'workContextChange',
53: }
54: 
55: export type Hooks = PluginHooks;
56: 
57: export interface PluginBaseCfg {
58:   theme: 'light' | 'dark';
59:   appVersion: string;
60:   platform: 'web' | 'desktop' | 'android' | 'ios';
61:   isDev: boolean;
62:   lang?: {
63:     code: string;
64:     [key: string]: unknown;
65:   };
66: }
67: 
68: export interface DialogButtonCfg {
69:   label: string;
70:   icon?: string;
71:   onClick?: () => void | Promise<void>;
72:   color?: 'primary' | 'warn';
73:   raised?: boolean;
74: }
75: 
76: export type DialogResult = string | undefined;
77: 
78: export interface DialogCfg {
79:   title?: string;
80:   /**
81:    * Rich HTML sanitized by the host before rendering, rebuilt from an allowlist.
82:    * Semantic HTML, native form controls and inline layout styles are preserved;
83:    * scripts, event-handler attributes, unsafe URLs, inline `<svg>` and `style`
84:    * values containing `url(` are removed. Escape untrusted values yourself.
85:    */
86:   htmlContent?: string;
87:   content?: string;
88:   okBtnLabel?: string;
89:   cancelBtnLabel?: string;
90:   buttons?: DialogButtonCfg[];
91: }
92: 
93: export interface SnackCfg {
94:   msg: string;
95:   type?: 'SUCCESS' | 'ERROR' | 'WARNING' | 'INFO';
96:   ico?: string;
97:   /**
98:    * Optional action button; the snack stays visible longer when set.
99:    * plugin.js only — functions cannot cross the iframe postMessage boundary.
100:    */
101:   action?: SnackActionCfg;
102: }
103: 
104: export interface SnackActionCfg {
105:   label: string;
106:   onClick: () => void;
107: }
108: 
109: export type SnackCfgLimited = SnackCfg;
110: 
111: export interface NotifyCfg {
112:   title: string;
113:   body: string;
114: }
115: 
116: export interface PluginNodeScriptConfig {
117:   allowedPaths?: string[]; // Specific paths the script can access
118:   timeout?: number; // Default timeout in milliseconds for scripts
119:   memoryLimit?: string; // Default memory limit (e.g., '128MB', '256MB')
120: }
121: 
122: export interface PluginNodeScriptRequest {
123:   script: string;
124:   timeout?: number;
125:   args?: unknown[];
126: }
127: 
128: export interface PluginNodeScriptError {
129:   code:
130:     | 'TIMEOUT'
131:     | 'MEMORY_LIMIT'
132:     | 'SCRIPT_ERROR'
133:     | 'PERMISSION_DENIED'
134:     | 'INVALID_SCRIPT'
135:     | 'NO_CONSENT';
136:   message: string;
137:   details?: {
138:     line?: number;
139:     column?: number;
140:     scriptSnippet?: string;
141:   };
142: }
143: 
144: export interface PluginNodeScriptResult {
145:   success: boolean;
146:   result?: unknown;
147:   error?: string | PluginNodeScriptError;
148:   executionTime?: number;
149:   resourceUsage?: {
150:     peakMemoryMB?: number;
151:     cpuTime?: number;
152:   };
153: }
154: 
155: export interface PluginManifest {
156:   name: string;
157:   id: string;
158:   manifestVersion: number;
159:   version: string;
160:   minSupVersion: string;
161:   description?: string;
162:   hooks: Hooks[];
163:   permissions: string[];
164:   /**
165:    * Exact hostnames this plugin is allowed to reach via `PluginAPI.request`
166:    * (e.g. `"api.example.com"`). Host-only, exact match — no wildcards, and the
167:    * port is ignored. Enforced by the host: a `request` to any host not listed
168:    * here is rejected. If omitted or empty, `PluginAPI.request` is disabled for
169:    * this plugin (fail-closed). Surfaced to the user at install so the plugin's
170:    * outbound network reach is reviewable. Does not affect issue-provider HTTP.
171:    *
172:    * Requires the `"http"` capability: `PluginAPI.request` only works if the
173:    * plugin ALSO declares `"http"` in `permissions`. Network egress is an
174:    * explicit, opt-in capability (like `nodeExecution`) — declaring hosts alone
175:    * does not grant it.
176:    *
177:    * Redirects: on web/desktop, `PluginAPI.request` refuses to follow HTTP
178:    * redirects (executes via `fetch` with `redirect: 'error'`), so a declared
179:    * host cannot 3xx the request onward to a non-allowlisted or private/metadata
180:    * host. On native (Capacitor), the platform HTTP layer still follows redirects
181:    * — that hop is not re-checked; treat native redirect-following as a known
182:    * limitation. DNS rebinding (hostname matched, not the resolved IP) also
183:    * remains out of scope.
184:    */
185:   allowedHosts?: string[];
186:   iFrame?: boolean;
187:   isSkipMenuEntry?: boolean;
188:   type?: 'standard' | 'issueProvider';
189:   assets?: string[];
190:   issueProvider?: IssueProviderManifestConfig;
191:   icon?: string; // Path to SVG icon file relative to plugin root
192:   nodeScriptConfig?: PluginNodeScriptConfig;
193:   sidePanel?: boolean; // If true, plugin loads in right panel instead of route
194:   uiKit?: boolean; // If false, skip injecting the UI kit CSS reset. Defaults to true.
195:   jsonSchemaCfg?: string; // Path to JSON schema file for plugin configuration relative to plugin root
196:   i18n?: {
197:     languages: string[]; // Array of supported language codes (e.g., ['en', 'de', 'fr'])
198:   };
199: }
200: 
201: // Hook payload types
202: export interface TaskCreatedPayload {
203:   taskId: string;
204:   task: Task;
205: }
206: 
207: export interface TaskCompletePayload {
208:   taskId: string;
209:   task: Task;
210: }
211: 
212: export interface TaskUpdatePayload {
213:   taskId: string;
214:   task: Task;
215:   changes: Partial<Task>;
216: }
217: 
218: export interface TaskDeletePayload {
219:   taskId: string;
220: }
221: 
222: export interface CurrentTaskChangePayload {
223:   current: Task | null;
224:   previous: Task | null;
225: }
226: 
227: export interface FinishDayPayload {
228:   date: string;
229: }
230: 
231: export interface LanguageChangePayload {
232:   code: string;
233:   newLanguage: string;
234: 
235:   [key: string]: unknown;
236: }
237: 
238: export interface ActionPayload {
239:   action: string;
240:   payload?: unknown;
241: }
242: 
243: export interface AnyTaskUpdatePayload {
244:   action: string;
245:   taskId?: string;
246:   task?: Task;
247:   changes?: Partial<Task>;
248: }
249: 
250: export interface ProjectListUpdatePayload {
251:   action: string;
252:   projectId?: string;
253:   project?: Project;
254:   changes?: Partial<Project>;
255: }
256: 
257: /**
258:  * Snapshot of the active work context (project or tag).
259:  * Used by getActiveWorkContext() and as the WORK_CONTEXT_CHANGE payload.
260:  *
261:  * **`taskIds` is a snapshot at the moment of emission**, not a live view.
262:  * It goes stale as soon as a task is added, removed, or moved. Plugins
263:  * that need the current ordering should call `getActiveWorkContext()` /
264:  * `getTasks()` on demand or subscribe to `ANY_TASK_UPDATE` for changes.
265:  */
266: export interface ActiveWorkContext {
267:   id: string;
268:   /**
269:    * `'TODAY'` is reported for the special Today tag (whose `id` is also
270:    * `'TODAY'`); every other tag is `'TAG'`. This matches the vocabulary of
271:    * {@link PluginWorkContextHeaderBtnCfg.showFor}.
272:    */
273:   type: 'PROJECT' | 'TAG' | 'TODAY';
274:   title: string;
275:   /**
276:    * An independent copy taken at emit time — safe to read, and mutating it
277:    * has no effect on the app. See the {@link ActiveWorkContext} note above.
278:    */
279:   taskIds: string[];
280: }
281: 
282: /**
283:  * Payload of the WORK_CONTEXT_CHANGE hook, fired when the user switches
284:  * between projects/tags. A context is always active while the app is
285:  * running, so the payload is never null.
286:  *
287:  * The included `taskIds` is a snapshot — re-read via `getActiveWorkContext()`
288:  * if you care about the current order/membership.
289:  */
290: export type WorkContextChangePayload = ActiveWorkContext;
291: 
292: // Map hook types to their payload types
293: export interface HookPayloadMap {
294:   [PluginHooks.TASK_CREATED]: TaskCreatedPayload;
295:   [PluginHooks.TASK_COMPLETE]: TaskCompletePayload;
296:   [PluginHooks.TASK_UPDATE]: TaskUpdatePayload;
297:   [PluginHooks.TASK_DELETE]: TaskDeletePayload;
298:   [PluginHooks.CURRENT_TASK_CHANGE]: CurrentTaskChangePayload;
299:   [PluginHooks.FINISH_DAY]: FinishDayPayload;
300:   [PluginHooks.LANGUAGE_CHANGE]: LanguageChangePayload;
301:   [PluginHooks.PERSISTED_DATA_CHANGED]: void;
302:   [PluginHooks.ACTION]: ActionPayload;
303:   [PluginHooks.ANY_TASK_UPDATE]: AnyTaskUpdatePayload;
304:   [PluginHooks.PROJECT_LIST_UPDATE]: ProjectListUpdatePayload;
305:   [PluginHooks.WORK_CONTEXT_CHANGE]: WorkContextChangePayload;
306: }
307: 
308: // Generic hook handler with typed payload
309: export type PluginHookHandler<T extends Hooks = Hooks> = (
310:   payload: T extends keyof HookPayloadMap ? HookPayloadMap[T] : unknown,
311: ) => void | Promise<void>;
312: 
313: // Core data types - Single source of truth for both plugins and app
314: export interface Task {
315:   id: string;
316:   title: string;
317:   notes?: string;
318:   timeEstimate: number;
319:   timeSpent: number;
320:   isDone: boolean;
321:   projectId: string | null;
322:   tagIds: string[];
323:   parentId?: string | null;
324:   created: number;
325:   updated?: number;
326:   subTaskIds: string[];
327: 
328:   // Additional fields for internal use (plugins can read but shouldn't modify)
329:   timeSpentOnDay?: { [key: string]: number };
330:   doneOn?: number | null;
331:   attachments?: any[];
332:   remindAt?: number | null;
333:   dueDay?: string | null;
334:   dueWithTime?: number | null;
335:   repeatCfgId?: string | null;
336: 
337:   // Issue tracking fields (optional)
338:   issueId?: string | null;
339:   issueProviderId?: string | null;
340:   issueType?: any | null; // IssueProviderKey in app
341:   issueWasUpdated?: boolean;
342:   issueLastUpdated?: number | null;
343:   issueAttachmentNr?: number;
344:   issuePoints?: number | null;
345: 
346:   // UI state (internal)
347:   _hideSubTasksMode?: number;
348: }
349: 
350: export interface Project {
351:   id: string;
352:   title: string;
353:   theme: {
354:     primary?: string;
355:     isAutoContrast?: boolean;
356:     [key: string]: unknown;
357:   };
358:   isArchived?: boolean;
359:   created?: number;
360:   updated?: number;
361:   taskIds: string[];
362:   backlogTaskIds: string[];
363:   noteIds: string[];
364:   isEnableBacklog?: boolean;
365:   isHiddenFromMenu?: boolean;
366: 
367:   // Advanced config (internal) - must be any to match WorkContextCommon
368:   advancedCfg: unknown;
369:   icon?: string | null;
370: }

418:  * Header button that is only rendered when the active work context matches
419:  * one of the entries in `showFor`. `'TODAY'` refers to the special TODAY tag.

421: export interface PluginWorkContextHeaderBtnCfg {

429: /**
430:  * OAuth configuration for starting an OAuth flow.
431:  *
432:  * Bring-your-own credentials: an issue-provider plugin may let users override the
433:  * clientId / clientSecret / redirectUri at runtime by writing them under
434:  * `pluginConfig.oauthOverrides = { clientId?, clientSecret?, redirectUri? }`. These
435:  * overrides apply only to the desktop (Electron loopback) flow and are ignored on web/native.
436:  */
437: export interface OAuthFlowConfig {
438:   authUrl: string;
439:   tokenUrl: string;
440:   clientId: string;
441:   /**
442:    * NOT kept confidential — this value is embedded in plugin source code,
443:    * persisted in user data, and may be synced to cloud backends.
444:    * Only use for OAuth providers that document their "client secret" as
445:    * non-confidential (e.g., Google installed-app credentials per RFC 8252).
446:    */
447:   clientSecret?: string;
448:   /**
449:    * Client ID for Android (authenticates via package name + SHA-1 signing key).
450:    * Overrides `clientId` on Android and omits `clientSecret`.
451:    * Requires "Custom URI scheme" enabled in Google Cloud Console.
452:    */
453:   mobileClientId?: string;
454:   /**
455:    * Client ID for iOS (authenticates via bundle ID).
456:    * Overrides `clientId` on iOS and omits `clientSecret`.
457:    * Requires "Custom URI scheme" enabled in Google Cloud Console.
458:    */
459:   iosClientId?: string;
460:   /**
461:    * Client ID for the web build, for providers that support public browser
462:    * clients via Authorization Code + PKCE without a client secret.
463:    * Overrides `clientId` in the browser (non-Electron, non-native) and omits
464:    * `clientSecret`.
465:    */
466:   webClientId?: string;
467:   scopes: string[];
468:   /** Additional query parameters to append to the authorization URL (e.g. access_type, prompt). */
469:   extraAuthParams?: Record<string, string>;
470:   /**
471:    * Optional redirect URI override for the desktop (Electron) loopback flow — e.g.
472:    * a user-supplied OAuth app that requires an exact pre-registered
473:    * `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/...` callback instead of the host default.

1: # Architecture Decision Records
2: 
3: This document tracks significant architectural decisions and patterns in the Super Productivity codebase. When making changes that affect these patterns, reference this document and update it if needed.
4: 
5: It is also the **index** of accepted decisions: a decision recorded somewhere else — because it is long enough to stand alone, or because it is enforced as a contributor rule — must still be listed under [Decisions Recorded Elsewhere](#decisions-recorded-elsewhere).
6: 
7: **Decisions:** [1. dueDay/dueWithTime Mutual Exclusivity Pattern](#1-duedayduewithtime-mutual-exclusivity-pattern) · [2. TODAY_TAG Virtual Tag Pattern](#2-today_tag-virtual-tag-pattern) · [3. Sync Package Boundary Direction](#3-sync-package-boundary-direction) · [4. Upload Conflict Safety via the lastSeq Row Lock Under RepeatableRead](#4-upload-conflict-safety-via-the-lastseq-row-lock-under-repeatableread) · [5. Project Completion: Decoupled Resolution over Atomic Multi-Entity Op](#5-project-completion-decoupled-resolution-over-atomic-multi-entity-op) · [6. Passkeys Stay Pending Until Email Verification](#6-passkeys-stay-pending-until-email-verification) · [7. Versioned Delete-Wins Semantics for Project Deletion](#7-versioned-delete-wins-semantics-for-project-deletion) · [8. Additive Data-Model Evolution over Schema Bumps](#8-additive-data-model-evolution-over-schema-bumps) · [9. Calendar Writes Live in Plugins, Behind Per-Provider Opt-In](#9-calendar-writes-live-in-plugins-behind-per-provider-opt-in) · [10. Vector Clocks over Server-Side Entity Versioning](#10-vector-clocks-over-server-side-entity-versioning)
8: 
9: ## Active Patterns & Decisions
10: 
11: ### 1. dueDay/dueWithTime Mutual Exclusivity Pattern
12: 
13: **Status**: ✅ Active (since commit `400ca8c1`, 2026-01-29)
14: 
15: **Decision**: The `task.dueDay` and `task.dueWithTime` fields are mutually exclusive in new data. When setting `dueWithTime`, `dueDay` must be cleared (set to `undefined`). When reading, `dueWithTime` takes priority over `dueDay`.
16: 
17: **Rationale**:
18: 
19: - Prevents state inconsistency bugs where both fields had conflicting values
20: - Single source of truth for task scheduling
21: - Simpler state management
22: 
23: **Implementation**:
24: 
25: - **Writing**: Clear `dueDay` when setting `dueWithTime` (in meta-reducers)
26: - **Reading**: Check `dueWithTime` first; only check `dueDay` if `dueWithTime` is not set (in selectors)
27: - **Legacy Data**: Old data with both fields works via priority pattern (no migration needed)
28: 
29: **Key Files**:
30: 
31: - [`task.model.ts`](src/app/features/tasks/task.model.ts) - Field definitions with JSDoc
32: - [`task-shared-scheduling.reducer.ts`](src/app/root-store/meta/task-shared-meta-reducers/task-shared-scheduling.reducer.ts) - Write implementation
33: - [`work-context.selectors.ts`](src/app/features/work-context/store/work-context.selectors.ts) - Read pattern
34: - [`planner.selectors.ts`](src/app/features/planner/store/planner.selectors.ts) - Read pattern
35: - [`task.selectors.ts`](src/app/features/tasks/store/task.selectors.ts) - Read pattern
36: 
37: **When to Update This Pattern**:
38: 
39: - Adding new date/time scheduling fields
40: - Modifying task scheduling logic
41: - Working with task selectors that check due dates
42: 
43: ---
44: 
45: ### 2. TODAY_TAG Virtual Tag Pattern
46: 
47: **Status**: ✅ Active (established pattern)
48: 
49: **Decision**: `TODAY_TAG` (ID: `'TODAY'`) is a **virtual tag** whose membership is determined by `task.dueWithTime` or `task.dueDay`, not by `task.tagIds`. The tag's `taskIds` field stores only the ordering of tasks, not membership.
50: 
51: **Key Invariant**: `TODAY_TAG.id` must NEVER be added to `task.tagIds`
52: 
53: **Rationale**:
54: 
55: - Uniform move operations across all tags (virtual and regular)
56: - Single source of truth for "today" membership (date fields, not tagIds)
57: - Self-healing ordering (stale entries automatically filtered)
58: - Natural integration with planner (which uses date fields)
59: 
60: **Related**: Uses the dueDay/dueWithTime mutual exclusivity pattern (Decision #1)
61: 
62: **Key Files**:
63: 
64: - [`tag.const.ts`](src/app/features/tag/tag.const.ts) - TODAY_TAG definition
65: - [`work-context.selectors.ts`](src/app/features/work-context/store/work-context.selectors.ts) - Membership computation
66: - [`task-shared-helpers.ts`](src/app/root-store/meta/task-shared-meta-reducers/task-shared-helpers.ts) - Invariant enforcement
67: 
68: **When to Update This Pattern**:
69: 
70: - Adding new virtual tags
71: - Modifying tag membership logic
72: - Working with today's task list
73: 
74: ---
75: 
76: ### 3. Sync Package Boundary Direction
77: 
78: **Status**: ✅ Active (since May 2026)
79: 
80: **Decision**: Operation-log sync code is split by dependency direction:
81: `src/app` composes host-specific wiring, `@sp/sync-providers` owns bundled
82: provider implementations, and `@sp/sync-core` owns framework-agnostic reusable
83: sync primitives.
84: 
85: **Rationale**:
86: 
87: - Keeps reusable sync algorithms independent of Angular, NgRx, app models, and
88:   provider implementations
89: - Prevents provider IDs, app action/entity enums, validation schemas, UI, OAuth,
90:   and platform bridges from leaking into the core engine package
91: - Gives boundary lint a clear rule: packages never import app code, and
92:   providers consume only public sync-core exports
93: 
94: **Implementation**:
95: 
96: - ESLint rejects Angular, NgRx, app, shared-schema, sync-core deep imports, and
97:   dynamic imports inside package sources
98: - `@sp/sync-core` owns the vector-clock algorithms that the app and the
99:   SuperSync server import directly; its only runtime dependencies are
100:   `@noble/ciphers` and `hash-wasm`, used by its encryption primitives
101: - `packages/shared-schema` owns schema contracts and validators shared by app
102:   and server and has no dependency on `@sp/sync-core`; `@sp/sync-core` must
103:   not import `@sp/shared-schema`
104: - `@sp/sync-providers` depends on public `@sp/sync-core` plus provider runtime
105:   helpers, while app factories inject credentials, platform bridges, validators,
106:   OAuth routing, and config
107: 
108: **Documentation**: [`docs/sync-and-op-log/package-boundaries.md`](docs/sync-and-op-log/package-boundaries.md)
109: 
110: **Key Files**:
111: 
112: - [`packages/sync-core/src/index.ts`](packages/sync-core/src/index.ts) - Core public API
113: - [`packages/sync-providers/package.json`](packages/sync-providers/package.json) - Provider public exports
114: - [`eslint.config.js`](eslint.config.js) - Package boundary enforcement
115: - [`src/app/op-log/sync-providers/sync-providers.factory.ts`](src/app/op-log/sync-providers/sync-providers.factory.ts) - App-side provider composition
116: 
117: **When to Update This Pattern**:
118: 
119: - Moving sync code between app and packages
120: - Adding a package export or dependency
121: - Adding a provider implementation or plugin-facing provider contract
122: - Changing vector-clock ownership or shared-schema compatibility
123: 
124: ---
125: 
126: ### 4. Upload Conflict Safety via the lastSeq Row Lock Under RepeatableRead
127: 
128: **Status**: ✅ Active (since May 2026; batch upload engine removed August 2026)
129: 
130: **Decision**: SuperSync uploads derive conflict-safety from the shared
131: `user_sync_state.lastSeq` row write that reserves server sequence numbers, not
132: from PostgreSQL RepeatableRead snapshot isolation alone.
133: 
134: **Note — batch upload engine deleted (2026-08, #9508)**: this decision was
135: originally written for the batch upload engine (`processOperationBatch`,
136: `prefetchLatestEntityOpsForBatch`, the `SUPERSYNC_BATCH_UPLOAD` flag). That
137: engine was never enabled in production and was deleted rather than rolled out;
138: the serial per-op path (`processOperation`) is the only upload engine. The
139: invariant below is engine-neutral and applies unchanged to the serial path.
140: The deleted batch code last lived at commit `924ddd7019`. Re-open condition:
141: the batch engine processed a 25-op upload in ~10 SQL statements vs ~127 for
142: serial — resurrect it (from that commit, re-reviewed) only if per-upload
143: latency or transaction lock-hold time becomes a measured production problem.
144: 
145: **Rationale**:
146: 
147: - PostgreSQL RepeatableRead does not provide full serializable snapshot isolation
148: - Two concurrent upload transactions can both pass conflict checks when they
149:   read the same pre-insert snapshot
150: - Reserving sequence numbers through one `user_sync_state.lastSeq` row forces
151:   accepted writers for the same user to serialize on that row lock
152: - A causal `REPAIR` snapshot must prove that its state includes the current
153:   server prefix; the same row serializes that base-cursor check with later writes
154: - If two uploads race, the later writer blocks on the row and the transaction
155:   retry path handles the serialization failure rather than silently accepting
156:   conflicting operations
157: - The serial path's post-allocation conflict re-check ("FIX 1.5", removed
158:   2026-08; last lived at commit `07511ab45c`) was dead code: under
159:   RepeatableRead both conflict checks read one snapshot fixed at the
160:   transaction's first statement, and the `lastSeq` increment raises a
161:   serialization failure (40001) against any committed concurrent upload
162:   before a re-check could run. Lowering the isolation level below
163:   REPEATABLE READ would require reinstating a post-allocation re-check.
164: 
165: **Implementation**:
166: 
167: - An upsert ensures the `user_sync_state` row exists (`lastSeq: 0`); each
168:   accepted operation then reserves its sequence number with an atomic
169:   `update({ lastSeq: { increment: 1 } })` on that row
170:   (`operation-upload.service.ts`)
171: - The operation insert uses `createMany(..., skipDuplicates: true)`: a lost
172:   duplicate-ID race surfaces as `count === 0` and is handled in-transaction
173:   (sequence rolled back, op classified as `DUPLICATE_OPERATION`) rather than
174:   aborting the whole upload with a unique-constraint error; only a non-ID
175:   unique conflict aborts the transaction
176: - `REPAIR` uploads persist `repairBaseServerSeq` on the operation row. The HTTP
177:   handler rejects an obviously stale base before quota cleanup, and the upload
178:   transaction repeats the check under `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` before insertion
179: - Regular uploads carrying `lastKnownServerSeq` use the same per-user row lock
180:   to reject an upload behind the latest `SYNC_IMPORT` or `BACKUP_IMPORT` before
181:   insertion. The durable replacement marker is reconciled lazily from retained
182:   operations for rows created before the marker existed.
183: - The marker carries **import** semantics — it forces a stale client to download
184:   a replacement whose concurrent ops the client then drops. Only an import
185:   advances it. The lazy reconcile falls back to the newest causal `REPAIR` purely
186:   as a stand-in for an import row that pruning already deleted; a repair is not a
187:   fence in its own right, and the client replays concurrent work on top of one
188:   rather than dropping it
189: - Markerless legacy repairs are compatibility records, not causal boundaries:
190:   they cannot drive download fast-forward, snapshot trust, history pruning, or
191:   server-generated restore points; snapshot replay across one fails closed
192: - Removing or sharding the `lastSeq` write requires replacing this safety
193:   mechanism with an equivalent per-user serialization primitive
194: 
195: **Documentation**:
196: [`packages/super-sync-server/docs/architecture.md`](packages/super-sync-server/docs/architecture.md),
197: [`docs/sync-and-op-log/sync-architecture.html#transport`](docs/sync-and-op-log/sync-architecture.html#transport)
198:

200:

216: ### 5. Project Completion: Decoupled Resolution over Atomic Multi-Entity Op
217: 
218: **Status**: ✅ Active (since 2026-06-06, branch `feat/completing-projects-48eeb4`)
219: 
220: **Decision**: "Complete project" is a **plain single-entity `PROJECT` flag flip** (`completeProject`, `OpType.Update`, mirroring `archiveProject` → sets `isDone`/`doneOn`/`isArchived`). The accompanying resolution of unfinished tasks ("move to Inbox" / "mark done") runs **first, as the normal per-task actions** (`moveToOtherProject` / `updateTask isDone`) dispatched in a loop with the Rule #6 bulk-dispatch flush — **not** bundled into a single atomic multi-entity op.
221: 
222: **Rationale**: An earlier iteration made completion one atomic `Batch` op (`completeProject`) that marked/moved tasks inside the project-shared meta-reducer. Because that op deliberately routed **around** the normal per-task actions, every system that observes those actions had to be re-taught about `completeProject` separately:
223: 
224: - **Conflict detection** needed a whole new `affectedEntities` multi-entity-ref feature threaded through sync-core, the sync server (+ a Prisma migration), shared-schema and the op-log — ~1,565 LOC, of which `completeProject` was the **only** producer.
225: - **Native-reminder cancellation**, **issue two-way-sync**, **time-block sync** and **repeat-cfg** effects each needed a dedicated `completeProject` listener to re-derive the task changes the atomic op skipped.
226: 
227: The atomic op's headline benefit — reversing the whole thing as one unit — was never realized: `reopenProject` only clears the project flags; it does **not** un-move or un-complete the resolved tasks. So the bundle paid a large cross-cutting cost for an undo guarantee it didn't provide. Decoupling makes the existing effects and per-entity conflict detection fire naturally and deletes ~1,750 LOC total (revert + decouple). Trade-off accepted: completion now emits **N+1 ops** (one per resolved task + the flag flip) instead of one, and there is a brief intermediate state — both fine for a rare, user-initiated action whose resolution is not atomically reversible anyway. One behavioral nuance vs. the old atomic op: when unfinished work is **moved to Inbox**, a task that was being actively tracked stays the current task (it was carried forward, not finished — consistent with Inbox's carry-forward intent); the **mark-done** path stops tracking the current task via the existing `autoSetNextTask$` effect. The atomic op cleared the current task in both cases; the decoupled design intentionally keeps it for the carry-forward case.
228: 
229: **Implementation**:
230: 
231: - **Action/reducer**: `completeProject({ id, doneOn })` in `project.actions.ts`; `on(completeProject)` flag flip in `project.reducer.ts` (guards `INBOX_PROJECT`). `reopenProject` clears the flags only.
232: - **Service**: `ProjectService.complete(id, doneOn)` dispatches the flag flip; `moveTasksToInbox()` / `markTasksDone()` loop the normal per-task actions + `setTimeout(0)` flush.
233: - **Flow**: `work-context-menu` resolves unfinished work **before** calling `complete()`.
234: - **Do NOT** reintroduce a multi-entity `completeProject` op or `affectedEntities` for it without re-justifying the full downstream cost above. Prior atomic implementation is preserved in history at commit `0893a86162`.
235: 
236: **Key Files**:
237: 
238: - [`project.actions.ts`](src/app/features/project/store/project.actions.ts), [`project.reducer.ts`](src/app/features/project/store/project.reducer.ts)
239: - [`project.service.ts`](src/app/features/project/project.service.ts) — `complete` / `moveTasksToInbox` / `markTasksDone`
240: - [`work-context-menu.component.ts`](src/app/core-ui/work-context-menu/work-context-menu.component.ts) — `completeProject()` flow
241:

243: 
244: - Adding a true bulk meta-reducer action for general use (revisit whether completion should adopt it)
245: - Reworking how completion resolves unfinished tasks
246: - Any proposal to make completion a single synced op again

250: ### 6. Passkeys Stay Pending Until Email Verification
251: 
252: **Status**: ✅ Active (since July 2026)
253: 
254: **Decision**: A passkey submitted during account registration is stored as a
255: `PendingPasskeyRegistration` tied to its exact email-verification token. It is
256: promoted to the user's active `Passkey` set only when that token is consumed.
257: 
258: **Rationale**:
259: 
260: - A WebAuthn registration ceremony proves possession of a credential, not
261:   ownership of the email address entered alongside it.
262: - Storing a submitted credential directly on an unverified user lets an attacker
263:   pre-register a victim's address, then have the victim's later magic-link
264:   verification activate the attacker's passkey.
265: - Keeping separate pending attempts prevents concurrent registrations from
266:   replacing or activating one another. The email owner chooses the credential
267:   by consuming the link produced by that same registration attempt.
268: - Failed email delivery leaves the bounded, expiring pending attempt in place.
269:   Deleting the shared unverified user can race a concurrent registration and
270:   invalidate a link that was successfully delivered.
271: 
272: **Implementation**:
273: 
274: - Passkey registration stores no active credential and creates one pending row
275:   per verification token.
276: - Email verification atomically claims the unverified user, replaces active
277:   passkeys with the credential bound to that token, and deletes the user's
278:   remaining pending attempts.
279: - Passkey verification tokens live only on pending registrations; user-row
280:   verification tokens belong to magic-link registrations. Consuming a user-row
281:   token verifies the email but removes untrusted active and pending passkeys.
282: - The migration moves the latest legacy credential for each unverified user to
283:   the pending table and removes all active credentials from unverified users.
284: - The resend cap bounds pending rows per unverified account; rows also expire
285:   with their verification tokens.
286: 
287: **Key Files**:
288: 
289: - [`auth.ts`](packages/super-sync-server/src/auth.ts)
290: - [`passkey.ts`](packages/super-sync-server/src/passkey.ts)
291: - [`schema.prisma`](packages/super-sync-server/prisma/schema.prisma)
292: 
293: **When to Update This Pattern**:
294: 
295: - Changing passkey enrollment or email-verification flows
296: - Adding another credential type to registration
297: - Changing verification-token persistence or cleanup

301: ### 7. Versioned Delete-Wins Semantics for Project Deletion
302: 
303: **Status**: ✅ Active (since July 2026)
304: 
305: **Decision**: Project deletions created with schema v4 or newer carry an explicit
306: `projectDeleteWins` marker and beat concurrent project updates. Historical,
307: unmarked deletions keep timestamp-based LWW semantics.
308: 
309: This is a deliberate semantic trade-off: a concurrent project rename or field
310: edit that is vector-clock CONCURRENT with a marked delete **loses**, regardless
311: of which has the newer wall-clock timestamp. Deleting an entity another device is
312: editing wins over the edit — the alternative (timestamp LWW) resurrects an empty
313: project shell and silently loses its task subtree. The lost edit is only
314: recoverable via local undo, not via sync.
315: 
316: **Rationale**:
317: 
318: - `deleteProject` is one user intent whose reducer cascade removes the project,
319:   active tasks, notes, sections, repeat configuration, and related archive data.
320:   Reversing only the project entity after that operation loses data and violates
321:   replay determinism.
322: - Capturing every cascaded entity in the delete payload or emitting restoration
323:   sidecars makes payload size scale with project size and still cannot restore
324:   every side effect safely.
325: - Deletion is the only complete, deterministic result already represented by the
326:   operation. A concurrent rename or project-field edit must not partially undo it.
327: - The schema-v4 barrier makes clients that do not understand this conflict policy
328:   stop before applying the operation (they block on the newer-schema gate rather
329:   than mis-resolving). The **absence** of the payload marker on historical
330:   deletions — never added by the no-op v3→v4 migration — is what preserves their
331:   timestamp-LWW semantics; the marker, not the version number, is the real
332:   discriminator. The classifier additionally requires the marked delete's
333:   plaintext `entityId` to match its authenticated payload `projectId`, so a
334:   tampered/replayed delete retargeted onto a live entity cannot win.
335: 
336: **Implementation**:
337: 
338: - New `deleteProject` actions include `projectDeleteWins: true`; replacement
339:   delete operations preserve that payload.
340: - The shared LWW planner accepts a host-supplied delete-wins classifier. A remote
341:   marked delete is applied regardless of timestamps. A local marked delete is
342:   replaced with one operation whose vector clock dominates both conflict sides.
343: - SuperSync keeps its generic conflict protocol: if the first delete upload is
344:   rejected, the existing retry path uploads the causally dominant replacement.
345:   File-based providers use the same client planner and marker.
346: - Do not add per-task/note restoration operations or project-sized snapshots to
347:   compensate a losing marked project delete.
348: 
349: **Key Files**:
350: 
351: - [`task-shared.actions.ts`](src/app/root-store/meta/task-shared.actions.ts) — the `PROJECT_DELETE_WINS_MARKER` producer
352: - [`conflict-resolution.ts`](packages/sync-core/src/conflict-resolution.ts)
353: - [`conflict-resolution.service.ts`](src/app/op-log/sync/conflict-resolution.service.ts) — the delete-wins classifier
354: - [`schema-version.ts`](packages/shared-schema/src/schema-version.ts)
355: - [`project-delete-wins-barrier-v3-to-v4.ts`](packages/shared-schema/src/migrations/project-delete-wins-barrier-v3-to-v4.ts) (registered in [`migrations/index.ts`](packages/shared-schema/src/migrations/index.ts))
356: 
357: **When to Update This Pattern**:
358: 
359: - Changing the cascade performed by `deleteProject`
360: - Adding another operation with delete-wins conflict semantics
361: - Changing schema compatibility or LWW replacement behavior

365: ### 8. Additive Data-Model Evolution over Schema Bumps
366: 
367: **Status**: ✅ Active (since August 2026)
368: 
369: **Decision**: Persisted and synced data evolves **additively**. Pick the change
370: channel by what actually changed (table below). Do not raise
371: `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` unless a change is **both** inexpressible as an additive
372: or derived field **and** would be _misapplied_ — not merely ignored — by older
373: clients. This is the constructive counterpart to the bump policy (sync rule 10),
374: which says when not to bump but not what to do instead.
375: 
376: | What changed                                                   | Channel                                                               | Precedent                                              |
377: | -------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
378: | Local storage layout (stores, indexes, derived meta)           | `DB_VERSION` ladder — local only, never transmitted                   | `db-upgrade.ts` v7 seeds the full-state-ops meta store |
379: | Shape of stored state (new field, legacy key, changed default) | Read-time normalization in the `loadAllData` reducer                  | `migrateFocusModeConfig`, `migrateKeyboardConfig`      |
380: | Representation of an existing **synced** field                 | Dual field — new field wins, legacy re-derived from it on every write | `normalizeStartOfNextDayConfig`                        |
381: | Semantics of an operation                                      | Payload marker / envelope, inert on older clients                     | `LwwUpdatePayload`; the v4 `projectDeleteWins` marker  |
382: 
383: **Rationale**:
384: 
385: - A bump fences only receivers that ship _after_ it. Released v17.0.0–v18.14.0
386:   clients apply ops up to schema 5 unmigrated and, at ≥ 6, block them while still
387:   advancing the cursor — permanently skipping them. A bump therefore never buys
388:   safety against the clients actually writing today's data.
389: - It cannot be reverted once any op carries the new version, and it hard-blocks
390:   every lagging post-v18.14.0 client on a frozen cursor.
391: - The legacy fleet does not age out on its own: there is **no desktop
392:   auto-updater** (the block in `electron/start-app.ts` is commented out) and the
393:   update banner's dismissal is persisted. Any policy gated on "wait for the old
394:   fleet to shrink" is a permanent no in disguise.
395: - Additive fields are safe by construction here: typia uses `createValidate`
396:   (excess properties are neither rejected nor stripped) and LWW patch application
397:   goes through `updateOne`, a shallow merge that retains unknown keys. **Renames
398:   and removals are the dangerous shape** — an old client that wins a conflict
399:   re-emits the entity without the field, destroying it fleet-wide — and no bump
400:   prevents that, because old clients keep writing regardless.
401: 
402: **Evaluation record (2026-08)**: raising `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` to 5 was
403: considered and **declined**. Neither candidate motivation survived: the
404: accumulated optional-field/runtime-default debt needs no migration (that pattern
405: _is_ the answer, per sync rule 11), and the typed RRULE recurrence model can ship
406: as an additive field while the flat fields stay canonical and re-derived — see
407: #9664, which also corrects that plan's inverted cross-version gate. A migration
408: with no payload is pure cost.
409: 
410: **Implementation**: no new machinery — each channel above already exists and has
411: a shipped precedent.
412: 
413: **Documentation**: [Bump Policy §A.7.11](docs/sync-and-op-log/operation-log-architecture.md#bump-policy--a-bump-does-not-protect-the-released-fleet), [`persisted-model-fields.md`](docs/sync-and-op-log/persisted-model-fields.md), `AGENTS.md` sync rules 10 and 11
414: 
415: **Key Files**:
416: 
417: - [`schema-version.ts`](packages/shared-schema/src/schema-version.ts) — the constant and its bump warning
418: - [`normalize-start-of-next-day-config.ts`](src/app/features/config/normalize-start-of-next-day-config.ts) — the dual-field template
419: - [`global-config.reducer.ts`](src/app/features/config/store/global-config.reducer.ts) — read-time normalization at `loadAllData`
420: - [`db-upgrade.ts`](src/app/op-log/persistence/db-upgrade.ts) / [`db-keys.const.ts`](src/app/op-log/persistence/db-keys.const.ts) — the local-only version ladder

430: ### 9. Calendar Writes Live in Plugins, Behind Per-Provider Opt-In
431: 
432: **Status**: ✅ Active (recorded 2026-08; describes the boundary that shipped 2026-03 in `3e2265fa57` / `020fd56504`)
433: 
434: **Decision**: Super Productivity is never the authority for calendar state. It
435: reads calendars to show the day's commitments, and it may write a _mirror_ of a
436: scheduled task back — but only through a **plugin issue provider** that opts into
437: the `timeBlock` contract, and only when the user has enabled that provider's
438: auto-time-blocking setting. Core code contains no calendar write path.
439: 
440: The boundary today:
441: 
442: | Surface                                                                                            | Writes?                           |
443: | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- |
444: | Built-in iCal/CalDAV URL feeds (`src/app/features/schedule/ical/`)                                 | No — poll and parse only          |
445: | Built-in issue providers (`src/app/features/issue/providers/*`)                                    | No — none implement `timeBlock`   |
446: | Plugin providers implementing `timeBlock` (`google-calendar-provider`, `caldav-calendar-provider`) | Yes, when `isAutoTimeBlock` is on |
447: 
448: **Rationale**:
449: 
450: - **A time block is a projection, not a synced entity.** `TimeBlockSyncEffects`
451:   pushes task state one way — schedule, reschedule, title, estimate, done, delete
452:   — into an event the app itself created. It never reconciles a user's edit of
453:   that event back into the task, and it never touches events the app did not
454:   create. That keeps the flow one-directional even though it writes, which is what
455:   avoids the sync loop a true bidirectional design has to solve.
456: - **Off by default, per provider.** `isAutoTimeBlock` is an unchecked box on the
457:   provider's config form. Writing into someone's calendar is not something to
458:   infer from an integration merely being connected (manifesto: opt-in, quiet by
459:   default).
460: - **Plugins are the right home.** Every write path needs OAuth, per-vendor event
461:   shapes, and vendor-specific throttling. Keeping that in `packages/plugin-dev/`
462:   behind the `timeBlock` contract means core carries no vendor API surface, and a
463:   broken provider degrades to read-only rather than breaking the app.
464: - **What is still excluded.** No reconciliation of external event edits into task
465:   state, no adoption of pre-existing calendar events, and no per-occurrence
466:   recurring-event editing (`RECURRENCE-ID`/`EXDATE`, #8148). These are the parts
467:   that would require answering conflict resolution between vector clocks and
468:   ETags, and they remain unbuilt — see #5001 for the open bidirectional request.
469: 
470: **Implementation**:
471: 
472: - Contract: `timeBlock: { upsertEvent, deleteEvent }` in
473:   [`packages/plugin-api/src/issue-provider-types.ts`](packages/plugin-api/src/issue-provider-types.ts)
474: - Driver: [`time-block-sync.effects.ts`](src/app/features/calendar-integration/time-block/time-block-sync.effects.ts),
475:   registered in [`feature-stores.module.ts`](src/app/root-store/feature-stores.module.ts)
476: - Manual per-event actions (reschedule, delete): [`calendar-event-actions.service.ts`](src/app/features/calendar-integration/calendar-event-actions.service.ts)
477: - Events themselves are **not** op-log entities — a converted task is an ordinary
478:   task with a derived stable id
479:   ([`generate-calendar-task-id.ts`](src/app/features/calendar-integration/generate-calendar-task-id.ts)).
480:   Provider _configuration_ does sync (`ISSUE_PROVIDER` in
481:   [`entity-registry.ts`](src/app/op-log/core/entity-registry.ts)).
482: 
483: **When to Update This Pattern**:
484: 
485: - A core (non-plugin) calendar write path is proposed — that crosses the boundary
486:   this record draws
487: - Reconciling external event edits back into task state is proposed (#5001) — that
488:   needs the ETag-vs-vector-clock conflict story written down first
489: - Per-occurrence recurring edits land (#8148)

493: ### 10. Vector Clocks over Server-Side Entity Versioning
494: 
495: **Status**: ✅ Active (recorded 2026-08; the alternative design is `git show 07511ab45c:docs/long-term-plans/server-side-entity-versioning.md`)
496: 
497: **Decision**: Conflict detection stays on **vector clocks**, pruned to
498: `MAX_VECTOR_CLOCK_SIZE = 20`. Server-side per-entity version counters (optimistic
499: concurrency control, the shape every centralized API uses) were designed in full
500: and are **not being built**. The design was never rejected on its merits by a
501: maintainer decision — it is recorded here as declined-by-default, because nothing
502: has yet justified its cost.
503: 
504: **Rationale**:
505: 
506: - **The problem it solves is not observed.** Pruning only discards causal
507:   information once 21+ distinct client IDs have touched a clock. For a personal
508:   deep-work tool that is not a realistic fleet, and the one edge case that did bite
509:   — an import client mispruning against its own ops — is already handled by a
510:   same-client check.
511: - **It would make the server the source of truth, not just the referee.** The
512:   SuperSync server already detects conflicts (`detectConflict` in
513:   `packages/super-sync-server/src/sync/conflict.ts`), but it does so by comparing
514:   clocks the _clients_ authored — the causal history stays client-owned. Entity
515:   versioning moves that authority into the server. File-based providers (WebDAV,
516:   Dropbox, local file) have no server to run it, so the vector-clock path must
517:   survive regardless, and we would maintain **two** conflict systems instead of
518:   one.
519: - **The migration is the expensive half.** It needs a new server table, a wire
520:   protocol change, a backfill for every existing entity, and a mixed-fleet window
521:   where old (clock-only) and new (version-carrying) clients edit the same entity.
522:   The design did address this — each step was independently deployable and
523:   backward compatible — but "correct on paper, across eight steps, in the
524:   subsystem where mistakes silently destroy user data" is precisely the cost being
525:   weighed, and there is no failure it currently buys us out of.
526: - **Encryption boundary.** The design assumed entity versions are non-sensitive
527:   and would ride outside E2EE. Plausible, but it adds another plaintext channel to
528:   reason about and was never re-derived against the current threat model — see
529:   [`supersync-encryption-architecture.md`](docs/sync-and-op-log/supersync-encryption-architecture.md).
530: 
531: **Implementation**: unchanged — see
532: [`docs/sync-and-op-log/vector-clocks.md`](docs/sync-and-op-log/vector-clocks.md).
533: The server prunes after conflict detection, before storage.
534: 
535: **When to Update This Pattern**:
536: 
537: - Real fleets are observed exceeding ~20 distinct client IDs per user, or pruning
538:   is traced to an actual user-visible conflict (rule: start from a reproducible
539:   problem)
540: - SuperSync becomes the only supported backend, removing the "file providers need
541:   the clock path regardless" constraint

559: ## How to Use This Document
560: 
561: ### When Making Architectural Changes
562: 
563: 1. **Before implementing**: Check if your change affects any active pattern
564: 2. **During implementation**: Follow the documented patterns
565: 3. **After implementation**: Update this document if you've:
566:    - Changed an existing pattern
567:    - Added a new architectural pattern
568:    - Made a decision that affects future development
569: 
570: ### When to Add a New Decision
571: 
572: Add a new decision record when:
573: 
574: - The decision affects multiple files/modules
575: - Future developers need to understand "why" not just "what"
576: - The pattern needs to be followed consistently across the codebase
577: - The decision prevents a specific class of bugs
578: 
579: ### When a Decision Changes
580: 
581: **Do not rewrite a record's rationale in place when the answer itself is reversed.** The reasoning history — why the old answer looked right, and what evidence flipped it — is the thing that stops the same idea being re-proposed a year later, and it is invisible in `git blame`. Instead:
582: 
583: 1. Set the old record's status to `❌ Superseded by #N` and **leave it where it is**. Numbering must stay stable: ~30 code comments cite decisions by number.
584: 2. Strip the superseded record down to **Decision** + **Rationale** — its _Implementation_ and _Key Files_ go stale the moment the code is gone — and add one line stating what new evidence or cost made it wrong.
585: 3. Write the replacement as a new numbered decision whose rationale names the record it supersedes.
586: 
587: No record has been superseded yet, so there is no worked example. Decision #5 is the closest model for the _content_ of step 2 — it records a rejected design, what it actually cost (~1,565 LOC of cross-cutting machinery for a single producer), why the headline benefit was never realized, and the commit (`0893a86162`) preserving the prior implementation. It is itself `✅ Active` and does not demonstrate the status/replacement mechanics of steps 1 and 3.
588: 
589: This applies only when the answer changes. Fixing wording, adding a key file, or clarifying an existing decision is ordinary editing.
590: 
591: ### Decision Record Template
592: 
593: ```markdown
594: ### N. [Pattern/Decision Name]
595: 
596: **Status**: ✅ Active | 🚧 Draft | ⚠️ Deprecated | ❌ Superseded by #N
597: 
598: **Decision**: [One-sentence summary of the decision]
599: 
600: **Rationale**:
601: 
602: - [Why was this decision made?]
603: - [What problems does it solve?]
604: 
605: **Implementation**:
606: 
607: - [How is it implemented?]
608: - [Key techniques or patterns used]
609: 
610: **Documentation**: [Link to detailed docs]
611: 
612: **Key Files**: [List of primary files implementing this pattern]
613: 
614: **When to Update This Pattern**: [Scenarios when someone should review/update this]
615: ```
616: 
617: ### Why One File
618: 
619: This log deliberately does **not** use one-file-per-decision (`docs/adr/NNNN-*.md`):
620: 
621: - The numbered records are one read for a contributor or an agent. Unlike the lint-enforced rules in [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md), a decision record's only teeth are being read — spreading them over 30 files means nobody reads all of them.
622: - `docs/` already separates plans, long-term-plans, research, sync-and-op-log and wiki. A further location makes decisions harder to find, not easier.
623: 
624: Note this is "one index, many locations", not "one file": [Decisions Recorded Elsewhere](#decisions-recorded-elsewhere) deliberately sanctions authoritative decisions living in their own documents. What stays consolidated is the **entry point**, so that ~30 in-code citations (`// See: ARCHITECTURE-DECISIONS.md Decision #2`) resolve to one place.
625: 
626: Revisit when supersession chains actually accumulate, or when this file passes ~1000 lines. Then split **by subsystem**, not one file per decision, and keep the existing numbering so those citations stay valid.

**Decision**: The `task.dueDay` and `task.dueWithTime` fields are mutually exclusive in new data. When setting `dueWithTime`, `dueDay` must be cleared (set to `undefined`). When reading, `dueWithTime` takes priority over `dueDay`.
- Prevents state inconsistency bugs where both fields had conflicting values
- Single source of truth for task scheduling
- **Reading**: Check `dueWithTime` first; only check `dueDay` if `dueWithTime` is not set (in selectors)
- **Legacy Data**: Old data with both fields works via priority pattern (no migration needed)
- Working with task selectors that check due dates

**Decision**: `TODAY_TAG` (ID: `'TODAY'`) is a **virtual tag** whose membership is determined by `task.dueWithTime` or `task.dueDay`, not by `task.tagIds`. The tag's `taskIds` field stores only the ordering of tasks, not membership.
**Key Invariant**: `TODAY_TAG.id` must NEVER be added to `task.tagIds`
- Uniform move operations across all tags (virtual and regular)
- Single source of truth for "today" membership (date fields, not tagIds)
- Natural integration with planner (which uses date fields)
**Related**: Uses the dueDay/dueWithTime mutual exclusivity pattern (Decision #1)
